title: Ethics Sheet for Automatic Emotion Recognition and Sentiment Analysis

bias_targets.methodology: The paper does not empirically measure bias, but rather serves as a theoretical ethics sheet. It proposes evaluating racial bias in Automatic Emotion Recognition (AER) systems by reporting disaggregated performance metrics across racial groups and testing for spurious correlations with identity terms.

As an ethics framework, the paper proposes evaluating gender bias by tracking systematic inaccuracies (e.g., systems incorrectly marking texts by women as more emotional) and recommends utilizing disaggregated performance metrics and diverse diagnostic datasets.

The paper recommends evaluating systemic disparities affecting neurodiverse populations (e.g., autism spectrum, alexithymia) by collecting participant information on neurodivergence (e.g., using the Toronto Alexithymia Scale) and reporting disaggregated performance metrics for these groups.

The paper discusses evaluating disparities in AER systems by tracking systemic inaccuracies for individuals with specific physical or mental health conditions, recommending disaggregation and context-specific dataset testing.
